column3: Close to the Greek.
The Greek asks what he wanted the child to be called, rather than directly what he wanted to name him.
“Zechariah” makes the unnamed subject explicit.
“Zechariah” supplies the pronoun’s referent, and “was released” supplies a distinct predicate for the tongue where the Greek coordinates it with the opened mouth.
The Greek literally speaks of fear coming on the neighbors and these words or events being discussed.
The Greek says they laid these things in their hearts; BSB renders this as wondering.
